## Oct 12 Results: Complete Whiff

Let's cut straight to the data. October 12 was a statistical disaster. We went 0-for-2, posting a 0.0% accuracy rate. When you miss on both picks in a two-game slate, there's no spinning the numbers. The model underperformed, and we need to examine what went wrong.

## The Data Breakdown

The Rays pick at 63% confidence was our highest conviction play, yet it failed to materialize. The Dodgers pick sat at exactly 50% - essentially a coin flip - and also missed. When your high-confidence pick (63%) performs identically to your low-confidence pick (50%), that's a red flag in the model's predictive variance. 

Sample size matters here. Two games is statistically insignificant for drawing long-term conclusions, but it's data we must acknowledge and learn from.

## Oct 13 Preview: Tomorrow's Top Pick

The model has recalibrated for October 13. We're running the same Guardians-Rays matchup back, but this time with different starting pitchers and updated variables.

## Pitcher Matchup Analysis

Freddy Peralta takes the mound for Tampa Bay against Cleveland's Parker Messick. The model gives the Rays a 53% edge - a modest advantage, but statistically meaningful. This isn't a high-conviction play like yesterday's 63% pick that missed, but the pitching matchup and home field advantage tilt the probability in Tampa Bay's direction.

Messick versus Peralta presents a clear differential in the data. While 53% represents only a slight edge, playoff baseball often comes down to marginal advantages. The model sees value here, even if it's not screaming confidence.

## The Bottom Line

Oct 12: 0-2, 0.0% accuracy. The numbers are what they are.

Oct 13: Backing the Rays at 53% with Peralta on the bump. Lower conviction than yesterday's miss, but the probability model still favors Tampa Bay.

We track every result, good or bad. That's how the data gets better.
